editorial:
Fifteen years after the original Woodsboro murders, Sidney Prescott comes back home to promote her new book about surviving trauma. But a new Ghostface killer shows up and starts targeting a fresh group of teens. You get to watch Sidney, Gale, and Dewey team up again while a new generation of kids tries to survive the chaos. The vibe is a fun mix of old-school slasher thrills and modern horror, with plenty of winks at horror movie rules and social media culture. It feels like a reunion party that suddenly turns deadly, and you never quite know who is behind the mask.

The acting is solid across the board, especially from the returning cast who slip right back into their roles. The pacing keeps things moving with good scares and a few laughs along the way. On the downside, some of the new teen characters feel a bit thin, and a couple of twists are easy to guess. Still, if you enjoy slasher movies with a smart, self-aware edge, this one is worth your time. endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn that Jill, Sidney's cousin, is the new Ghostface killer. She teamed up with her friend Charlie to create a new massacre so she could become famous like Sidney. Jill kills Charlie and stabs Sidney, but Sidney survives. Jill tries to frame herself as the sole survivor, but Sidney fights back and kills her. The movie ends with Sidney, Gale, and Dewey alive, while Jill's plan for fame falls apart completely.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slasher movies with a smart, self-aware edge.
